What it is and what you need

With PC control you operate a Windows computer from the phone as if you had its keyboard in your hands: each gesture on the control screen sends a key or a combination to the PC, and whatever the PC screen reader says you hear here, with the Tiresias voice.

You need: on the PC, Windows with NVDA 2025.1 or later (Remote Access is built in), or an older NVDA with the NVDA Remote add-on, or Tiresias for Windows. On the phone, Tiresias active. And both need the Internet or the same Wi-Fi.

You do not need to know braille: the control screen uses one- to four-finger gestures. If you prefer braille, the braille surface is still there (Settings, Braille, “When connecting to a PC”).

On the PC, with NVDA: open the NVDA menu (NVDA plus N), Tools, Remote Access, Connect (or press NVDA plus Alt plus R). If you do not see Remote Access, enable it in Settings, Remote Access, “Enable Remote Access”.

In the dialog choose “Allow this computer to be controlled”. For Server, “Use existing” and type nvdaremote.com (or your own server). For Key, a long, hard-to-guess key, or press “Generate key”. Press OK. NVDA says it is connected to the server.

If both are on the same Wi-Fi you can choose “Host locally”: the PC is the server, on port 6837; on the phone you will type the PC's IP address. It is the most private option: nothing leaves your home.

To avoid doing this every time, in Settings, Remote Access, check “Automatically connect after NVDA starts” with the same details. To pass the details to the phone without typing them, in Tools, Remote Access, “Copy link”: paste it into a message and open or copy it on the phone.

With Tiresias for Windows the path is the same in its remote access menu.

Important: whoever has the server and the key controls your PC. Do not share it, and change it if you have sent it to someone.

On the phone, in the Tiresias side menu, “Control a PC with NVDA”. Press “Connect to a PC”, type the server (nvdaremote.com, or the PC's IP with a colon and the port if it is not 6837) and the same key as on the PC. Or, if you copied the nvdaremote link, “Paste an nvdaremote link”.

If Tiresias asks about the server certificate (with your own server or the direct connection), trust it only if it is yours. The status is said at the top: “Connected to the PC” means it is done. “In the channel, but the PC is not there” means the key is not the same or the PC has not yet chosen “Allow this computer to be controlled”.

When the PC comes in, the control screen comes up by itself. To avoid typing it all again, “Save this computer”: the key is stored encrypted on the phone, and next time you choose the computer and Connect.

The control screen fills the whole phone and is black: there is nothing to explore, all of it is for gestures. Gestures are made with one, two, three or four fingers, and come in five kinds: one tap, two taps in a row, three taps, hold (keep the fingers still for half a second) and swipe to a side, up or down.

The rule to remember: one finger is the most used (arrows, Enter, silence); two fingers, Tab, Escape and the context menu; three fingers, windows and the command menu; four fingers, start and end, status and removing the screen.

To remove it: four fingers with two taps, or both volume keys at once. The screen does not go away when you switch apps or turn the phone off (depending on Settings, Braille, “When locking the phone”), but it does after five minutes without touching it. To put it back, in Control a PC, “Put up the control screen”, or assign the “PC control screen” action to a gesture.

If the PC talks too much, one tap with one finger silences it.

One finger left, right, up or down are the keyboard arrows: with them you go through menus, lists and text.

Two fingers to the right is Tab, and to the left, Shift plus Tab: that is how you move from one control to the next in windows and dialogs (buttons, check boxes, fields). It is the key you will use most.

Two taps with one finger is Enter: it presses the button, opens the file or the menu option. Three taps with one finger is Space: it checks and unchecks boxes. Two fingers up is Escape: it closes the menu or dialog without doing anything. Two fingers down is the context menu (what the right mouse button shows). One finger held is Alt: it goes to the program's menu bar; then move with the arrows and accept with two taps.

Try it: two fingers held open the Start menu; dictate what you are looking for (two fingers, two taps) and accept with two taps of one finger.
This is the whole table. Come back here whenever you want to review it; inside the control screen, three fingers held open it as a menu.

Three fingers up is “say all”: NVDA reads from where it is to the end, and one tap with one finger stops it. Two fingers with three taps read the current line. Three fingers with one tap say the window title (to know where you are). Two fingers with one tap say what has focus.

In the command menu, NVDA category, there is more: the status bar, the time and date, reading the PC clipboard, text formatting, the elements list, NVDA settings and changing the speech mode (talk, beeps, off or on demand).

What the PC says is heard with the Tiresias voice and in its language. If you want to mute it for a while (to attend to the phone), four fingers with three taps mute the PC voice and bring it back. And if you want Tiresias to say each command it sends (“Tab”, “Enter”), turn it on in Settings, Braille, or in the command menu, “This screen”.

Three fingers to the right is Alt plus Tab: it goes to the next window; to the left, to the previous one. If you have many open, in the command menu, Modifiers, “Hold Alt down” lets you go through them with Tab one by one and hear each one; when done, “Release Alt”.\n\nIn the command menu, Windows category, is the rest: the Start menu, go to the desktop, File Explorer, Run, Search, Settings, close the window (Alt plus F4), the window menu, maximize and minimize, the taskbar, the notification area, browser tabs, lock the PC and Control plus Alt plus Delete. The latter only works with NVDA installed (not the portable version) and may be limited by the PC\'s configuration.

There are three ways to type on the PC. Two fingers with two taps is dictation: speak and what you said is pasted where the PC cursor is. Three fingers with two taps open the phone keyboard: the control screen steps aside while you type, and comes back by itself when you accept. Three fingers with three taps paste on the PC whatever you have copied on the phone.

From the PC to the phone: in NVDA, Tools, Remote Access, “Send clipboard” sends what is copied on the PC to the phone, and Tiresias announces it.

To correct: four fingers to the left is Backspace; to the right, Delete; up, Home (start of the line); down, End. In the command menu, Editing and text, are copy, cut, paste, undo, select all, save, find, moving by words and selecting by characters, words and lines. For a single letter or a shortcut with a letter, Single keys, Letters (or Numbers and Function keys).

Three fingers down open the command menu, with everything that has no gesture of its own, by category: Windows, Editing and text, NVDA, Object navigation, Review cursor, Web navigation, Single keys, Modifiers, Gestures of this screen and This screen.

Inside the menu, one finger right or down goes to the next option and left or up to the previous one; one tap repeats the option; two taps choose it (and the menu closes); two fingers left go back to the category; two fingers up (or three down) close the menu; three fingers up go to the first option.

Modifiers (Control, Alt, Shift, Windows and the NVDA key) are armed for the next key: choose Control in Modifiers and then, in Single keys, Letters, S: that is Control plus S, Save. You can arm several. Four fingers with one tap say the status, with the armed modifiers; in Modifiers, “Remove the armed modifiers” releases them.

On web pages NVDA has two modes. In browse mode you read the page with the arrows, line by line, and jump by element type with quick keys. In focus mode you type in fields and use controls as in a program. NVDA switches by itself when entering a field; to switch by hand, in the command menu, Web navigation, “Toggle browse mode and focus mode” (NVDA plus Space).

The quick keys are in Web navigation: headings (and by level, 1 to 6), links, buttons, form and edit fields, check boxes, combo boxes, lists, tables, landmarks, graphics and more. Two taps go to the next of that kind; two fingers to the right, to the previous one. In tables, cells are visited with “Cell to the right”, “to the left”, “below” and “above”.

The elements list (NVDA plus F7) shows all the links, headings or fields of the page: go through it with the arrows and accept with two taps. To find text on the page, “Find on the page”, dictate or type, and Enter. To go to an address, “Address bar” (Control plus L), dictate or type the address and Enter. “Previous page” is Alt plus left arrow.

When Tab does not reach something (loose text, a notice), NVDA has object navigation: in the command menu, Object navigation, are the current object, the container, the previous and next ones, the first one inside, activating the object and going back to focus.

The review cursor reads text anywhere without moving the real cursor: in Review cursor, previous, current and next lines, words and characters, the start and the end, say all from there and copying a chunk (“Mark the start” and “Copy up to here”).

These commands depend on the NVDA keyboard layout on the PC: desktop (with numeric keypad) or laptop. Set the same one NVDA has (in NVDA, Settings, Keyboard, “Keyboard layout”) in Settings, Braille, “NVDA keyboard layout on the PC”, or change it in the command menu, This screen.

“No PC is connected”: check the status in Control a PC. If it says “In the channel, but the PC is not there”, the PC is missing “Allow this computer to be controlled” or the key is not the same.

The PC cannot be heard: four fingers with three taps bring the PC voice back if you had muted it; four fingers held change the NVDA speech mode (if it is “off” or “on demand” it does not talk); and raise the Tiresias voice volume.

Keys do strange things: four fingers with one tap say whether a modifier is armed or Alt is held; in the command menu, Modifiers, “Remove the armed modifiers” and “Release Alt”.

I cannot get into the sign-in screen or administrator prompts: NVDA must be installed on the PC (not portable) and with “Use NVDA during sign-in” checked in its general settings; Control plus Alt plus Delete may not work depending on the PC's configuration.

The screen goes away: after five minutes without touching it, it removes itself; put it back from Control a PC or with the “PC control screen” action. When locking the phone, by default it disconnects (Settings, Braille, “When locking the phone with a PC connected”). The control screen needs Android 11 or later.

Security: the relay server sees what happens; use a trusted one or the direct connection. To cut off, in the command menu, This screen, “Disconnect from the PC”, or on the Control a PC screen.

You now know everything you need: preparing the PC, connecting, moving around, reading, windows, typing, the command menu, the web, objects and what to do if something fails.\n\nThe button below puts up the control screen without a PC: each gesture is said and not sent, the command menu opens the same and nothing goes anywhere. Practice until the gestures come out without thinking; to leave, four fingers with two taps or both volume keys. Then connect to your PC from Control a PC with NVDA.
